correctness.rationale: For arbitrary odd q and nonsquare delta, the z-fiber is multiplication by alpha=1+beta z, of nonzero norm. The alpha values are exactly the distinct trace-two roots; each nonzero fiber contributes one fixed point and uniform orbits on its q^2-1 nonzero points. This yields the exact global gcd/Mobius cycle law. A primitive d<=15 requires q to be a nontrivial involution modulo d, leaving only 8,12,15; exact integer resultants and four degree-two modular gcd computations show the stated characteristics and precisely two z-fibers each. Parity follows from quadratic determinant characters and the determinant product 4. The standalone checker reproduces 16 exact certificates, 132 prime-power root-count checks and 224 prime-field fiber tests. Finite checks are supporting evidence only.

value.rationale: The period cutoff is structural, not an arbitrary finite sample: 8,12,15 are precisely the first moduli with nontrivial involutions in their unit groups, so these are the first potentially occurring nontrivial periods. The exact characteristic and extension-parity restrictions give the sharp arithmetic boundaries and exact cycle counts for an existing natural quadratic map. General cycle computation methods do not directly supply that explicit initial spectrum.
